sections.h2: What should a seller in Caledonia, WI know first?
sections.html:
Caledonia is a village in the northeast corner of Racine County, with 25,361 residents at the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate of 25,229 on July 1, 2025. Selling a house here means dealing with the village for assessment and permit history, and with Racine County for recording the deed.

Your realistic options are a listing with an agent, a sale by owner, or a direct sale to a cash buyer. Which one fits depends on the condition of the house, whether it sits in the village's older neighborhoods or on a larger rural lot, and how soon you need to close.

sections.h2: How is Caledonia laid out, and why does it matter for a sale?
sections.html:
The village covers about 45 square miles along Lake Michigan, which makes it large by Wisconsin standards. It is made up of distinct communities: Franksville (the old Skunk Grove trading area), Husher, Tabor and others that began as trading posts, railroad stops and crossroads, according to the village's own history page. A buyer looking at a Franksville lot is comparing a different setting from someone looking near Douglas Avenue, and your listing or offer conversation should reflect that.

The village describes easy access to I-94, with Milwaukee 18 miles north and Chicago 73 miles south, plus two business parks (Caledonia and DeBack Farms) that supply local jobs. It also notes the planned Microsoft development in neighboring Mount Pleasant. Commute length matters to buyers, and Census data puts the mean travel time to work for Caledonia residents at 25.8 minutes.

The land has deep roots. An Indian-French fur trader, Jacques Vieau, ran a trading post here around 1832, the Town of Caledonia was created by a territorial act on February 7, 1842, and Bohemian farmers settled in the Tabor area from 1849. The area became a village in January 2006, after a 2005 referendum. For an owner, that history shows up as older farmhouses, long narrow lots near the lakeshore and mixed rural and suburban parcels.

sections.h2: How does the Caledonia assessor affect your sale?
sections.html:
The village has contracted its assessing since 1999 through Cole-Layer-Trumble, now Tyler Technologies. The assessor's job is to place market-based values on all taxable property, and the village states that the assessor does not set tax rates or collect taxes.

  • The village published an assessment ratio of 0.9533 for 2025.
  • The assessor's public hours are Thursdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and clerical staff answer questions Monday through Wednesday mornings.
  • A 2026 preliminary assessment list by address and a 2026 Guide for Property Owners are posted on the assessor page.

The 2026 appeal window has closed. Notices went out July 1, the open-book period ran July 13 to 31, the deadline to give notice of objection was August 17, and the Board of Review met August 19. If you think an assessment is too high before you list, ask the assessor's office when next year's schedule is set. An objection must be filed on form PA-115A at least 48 hours before the first Board of Review meeting, unless the board waives it for good cause.

sections.h2: What permits and building records come up in Caledonia?
sections.html:
The village Building Department issues permits for residential and commercial work, with building, electrical and plumbing inspectors on staff. New homes go through the State of Wisconsin online building permit system, and plumbing and electrical permits are pulled separately from the main application.

For a sale, the practical point is that any work on the house since you bought it should have a closed permit. A buyer's lender or inspector may ask for it, and open work can lower an offer. Call the Building Department with the parcel address and ask for the permit history before you list.

  • A septic mound system needs a sanitary permit from Racine County Planning and Development, so ask that office for records if your lot has one.
  • Rural and lakeshore parcels can have drainage, grading and culvert certifications on file, which the village requires for new homes.
  • Keep copies of final inspection sign-offs with your sale file.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed at the Racine County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Caledonia deeds are recorded in Racine County. The county's flat recording fee for a standard document is $30, plus the state transfer fee on the sale. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor owes 30 cents per $100 of value, and on a land contract the value is the total principal the buyer agrees to pay.

The Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return can only be filed online through the Department of Revenue. The Register of Deeds can't help complete it; the county points people to the Department of Revenue at (608) 264-6885 or (608) 266-1594. A deed must also meet the county's checklist:

  • Grantor and grantee are named
  • The grantor's signature is notarized or authenticated
  • A complete legal description is included
  • The parcel identification number is shown
  • The drafter's name and a return address appear on the document
  • The document is legible and follows the state margin rules

The Racine County Register of Deeds phone number is (262) 636-3208. If the owner has died and the deed lists the decedent, ask whether a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest (form HT-110, $30 to record) applies before you sell.

sections.h2: What disclosure does Wisconsin require when you sell in Caledonia?
sections.html:
Most sellers must give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, under Wis. Stat. 709.02. The chapter covers property with one to four dwelling units, and it also covers land with no buildings, which uses a separate vacant land report. That second category matters in a village with rural parcels.

A buyer who does not receive the report on time can rescind within two business days after the 10-day period ends and get any deposit back. Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the property are not required to give the report. Everyone else should answer every item, since a report counts as complete only when each item is answered or covered by a permitted substitute.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale or a listing better in Caledonia?
sections.html:
A listing makes sense when the house is current on repairs and you can wait for a buyer's financing. A cash sale makes more sense when the house needs work, has a short payoff clock, or comes with tenants or an estate to settle.

Compare offers on net proceeds rather than price alone. Ask the title company to show the payoff, the transfer fee, the $30 recording fee, prorated taxes and any repair credit. If the number you would net from a listing is not much higher than a clean cash offer, the faster route can win.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a house in Caledonia?
faqs.a: Record it with the Racine County Register of Deeds. The flat recording fee is $30, and the Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return must be filed online with the Department of Revenue first.

faqs.q: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Caledonia sale?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents per $100 of value, charged to the seller. A $250,000 sale carries a $750 fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Caledonia assessment?
faqs.a: No, the 2026 deadline to give notice of objection was August 17, 2026, and the Board of Review met August 19. Ask the village assessor's office for next year's dates.

faqs.q: Do I need a condition report to sell a house in Caledonia?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Chapter 709 gives you 10 days after the contract is accepted to deliver it, and the buyer may rescind if it is late. Fiduciaries who never lived in the home are excused.
The village has contracted with Cole-Layer-Trumble, now Tyler Technologies, since 1999. The assessor's office keeps public hours on Thursdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
